answer: Before a new agent takes a seat, the ledger makes it post a small refundable bond and solve a unique work puzzle, so one operator cannot cheaply print a fleet of clones. Sybil mass becomes expensive: each fake identity pays real stake and real compute per identity, and if the fleet votes as one the bonds can be slashed together. Identity comes from cost, not from a self-issued name like a caravan badge on a voyage, and honest peers treat the bond pool as timber that props the roof while the oasis of cheap talk stays fenced outside.
